headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors if OpenHands processes PaddleOCR outputs as trusted document content; shared runtime writes also create moderate conflict risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write files, run browsers, and use MCP, so it may ingest PaddleOCR-produced document text or browser output as trusted input. PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can emit extracted text that may contain attacker-controlled instructions. The pair has a plausible shared-file bridge via OpenHands mounted volumes, but no documented provenance tracking is shown.
conditions: IF OpenHands reads PaddleOCR output from a shared file or MCP channel without provenance checks, injected instructions can be followed.
IF PaddleOCR extracts text from adversarial documents, that text can reach OpenHands as trusted content.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every PaddleOCR output file before OpenHands reads it.
Require OpenHands to treat OCR text as untrusted data, not instructions.
Separate input and instruction channels in the shared workspace.
Review one sample document flow for prompt-injection markers.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands has broad filesystem access and broad network egress, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images. If both touch the same mounted workspace, sensitive document contents can flow from B into A and then out through A's networked tools or model provider. The profiles do not show isolation or redaction by default, so leakage is plausible in default pair usage.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted documents, OpenHands can read the OCR inputs and outputs.
IF OpenHands forwards those contents to a model provider or external API, document data can leave the workspace.
mitigations: Restrict OpenHands to a redacted copy of the workspace.
Disable network egress for runs that process sensitive documents.
Keep OCR inputs and agent prompts in separate directories.
Inspect one run for unexpected file reads before enabling batch use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands can write the filesystem and modify git state; PaddleOCR can also operate on files in the same workspace. That creates overlapping writes to shared mutable resources, especially if OCR outputs are committed or rewritten in place. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so conflict risk exists beyond read-only overlap.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR writes extracted text into the same directory OpenHands edits, file clobbering can occur.
IF OpenHands commits or rewrites OCR outputs without locks, git state can diverge.
mitigations: Use separate output directories for OCR and coding tasks.
Pause one agent while the other writes shared files.
Commit OCR outputs only after manual review.
Check for file diffs before each OpenHands write.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspace and git operations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can act on files and browser output, so if it consumes PaddleOCR text as authoritative, OCR mistakes can cascade into edits, commits, or web actions. PaddleOCR is a document-processing system, not a verifier, and the profiles show no built-in cross-check between them. The interaction is therefore a default-pathway error chain rather than a guarded handoff.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses PaddleOCR output as ground truth, OCR errors can propagate into code or document changes.
IF OpenHands commits or acts on those outputs, the downstream mistake becomes persistent.
mitigations: Require a human review step before OpenHands acts on OCR output.
Compare OCR output against the source image for one sample page.
Mark OCR text as tentative in filenames or metadata.
Limit OpenHands to read-only analysis for the first pass.
requires-engineering: add verification heuristics before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications or residency constraints, so no specific compliance breach is evidenced. However, OpenHands handles model-provider API keys and broad egress while PaddleOCR processes documents/images, so a compliance mismatch could arise if regulated documents are routed through the pair. The other agent is not cited because no residency or certification data is provided for it.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through the pair, OpenHands' external egress may create a policy mismatch.
IF the operator requires residency or retention guarantees, neither profile documents them.
mitigations: Avoid regulated documents in this pairing.
Confirm retention settings for any external model provider.
Store OCR outputs in a local-only workspace.
Review vendor policies before production use.
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention controls.
